The test image shows a microscopic view with:
- Dark brown/black septate branching hyphae (stolons)
- Round black sporangia on stalks (sporangiophores)
- Classic pin-mold morphology

This strongly suggests **Rhizopus** (with characteristic sporangia). Let me compare with reference images across 4 classes.
Same Bugwood source series (5369117 vs 5369128 in test). Now checking Alternaria for comparison.
Alternaria shows conidiophores with club-shaped conidia - nothing like the test. Now checking Gray_Mold and Sclerotinia for completeness.

The 4th reference image (Bugwood_11.jpg from Rhizopus_Soft_Rots) is **identical** to the test image — same Bugwood ID 5369128, same microscopic structures: thick dark amber stolons with characteristic round black sporangia on sporangiophores. This is classic *Rhizopus* pin-mold morphology.

- Gray_Mold: clusters of tiny pale conidia — no match
- Alternaria: club-shaped multicellular conidia on conidiophores — no match
- Rhizopus: globose black sporangia on brown sporangiophores with stolons — exact match
